title: Docker:
do you actually
need it?
slides.subtitle: Your AI tool says “install Docker”. Here is when to listen.

slides.label: The pain
slides.detail: Your AI coding tool says “install Docker” and you have no idea why. Or the app works on your laptop and breaks everywhere else.
slides.start: Both have the same fix, and you might not need it.

slides.label: Docker is a lunchbox
slides.detail: A toy brick castle falls apart at a friend's house: different bricks, wobbly table. Pack it in a lunchbox with every brick and its own little table, and it stands up anywhere.
slides.start: Docker packs your app with everything it needs, so it runs the same on any computer.

slides.label: Why your AI asks for it
slides.detail: Your AI tool does not need Docker. Some of your project's tools do. Supabase runs a full copy of your backend (database, logins, storage) on your laptop using Docker.
slides.start: If Docker is not running, that setup fails, so the AI asks you to install it.

slides.label: A safe practice copy
slides.detail: On the copy, the AI can test, break things and reset without touching your real users or live data.
slides.start: Mistakes happen on the copy. Only finished, tested changes go live.

slides.label: The one-question rule
slides.detail: Ask this at the start of every project:
slides.quote: If the AI makes a mistake here, could it damage data I care about?
slides.start: Yes: use Docker or a separate test project. No: keep it simple and skip it.

slides.label: Use it when you have
slides.detail: A database you will test against (Supabase, Postgres, MySQL, Redis). Several pieces running together (website, API, database). Plans to deploy as a container (Fly.io, Railway, Cloud Run, a VPS).
slides.start: The database is the big one.

slides.label: Skip it for
slides.detail: Landing pages and static sites. Frontend-only apps that call hosted APIs. Simple scripts and automations. Quick prototypes. Sites on Vercel or Netlify.
slides.start: Add it later if the project grows a real database.

slides.label: Two honest caveats
slides.detail: Docker Desktop can use a few GB of memory, so quit it when a project does not need it. The local copy starts empty: it is for testing, not a replacement for your real database or hosting.
slides.start: Docker is a practice space, not your live app.

title: One question.
Then build.
slides.body: Building with AI and not sure which side of the line your project sits? Our first conversation is free.
slides.cta: What's the most confusing thing your AI coding tool has asked you to install?
